message: New here? `codemie setup` walks you through picking a provider (SSO, LiteLLM, Bedrock, Ollama...) — takes about a minute.
Config gone sideways? `codemie setup --force` reruns the wizard from scratch.
Juggling work and personal projects? `codemie profile` keeps separate setups for each and lets you hop between them.
Hop between setups with `codemie profile switch work` — run it bare and you get an interactive picker.
On AI/Run CodeMie SSO? `codemie profile login` authenticates you against your CodeMie URL — no API keys to juggle.
Not sure what is installed? `codemie list` lays out every available agent and framework.
Only care about this machine? `codemie list --installed` filters the catalog down to what is actually set up.
You are not limited to one agent — `codemie install <agent>` adds claude, gemini, codex, kimi and friends.
Pinpoint control: `codemie install claude 2.0.30` grabs that exact version, while `codemie install claude --supported` picks the one CodeMie tested.
Cleaning house? `codemie uninstall <agent>` tidies away agents you no longer use.
Worth running `codemie update` once in a while — it brings your installed agents up to their recommended versions.
Look before you leap: `codemie update --check` lists what is outdated without installing, and `codemie update claude` updates just one agent.
The CLI itself keeps improving too — `codemie self-update` gets you the latest features and fixes.
Zero install needed: the built-in agent is already here — try `codemie-code "explore this repo"` or a quick `codemie-code health`.
Every installed agent gets its own binary — `codemie-claude`, `codemie-gemini`, `codemie-codex` — same flags as the native tool, CodeMie wiring included.
OpenWiki writes a living wiki for your repo: `codemie install openwiki` once, then `codemie-openwiki --init`, and keep it fresh with `codemie-openwiki --update`.
These hints rotate at session start and end — run `codemie tips` anytime to browse them all at once.
Just updated? `codemie whatsnew` shows what changed in your version.
Claude Desktop, VS Code or Codex Desktop? `codemie proxy connect --claude-desktop` (or `--vscode`, `--codex-desktop`) routes them through your CodeMie profile.
On VS Code Insiders? `codemie proxy connect --vscode --insiders` targets it instead of the stable build.
The Claude Code extension for VS Code works too — `codemie proxy connect --vscode-claude-code` points it at your CodeMie profile.
Borrow another profile for one run: `codemie proxy connect --claude-desktop --profile work` uses its credentials without switching globally.
Claude Desktop acting up? `codemie proxy inspect desktop` shows proxy state, recent sessions and sync readiness.
Is the local gateway even alive? `codemie proxy status` tells you — add `--deep` to verify upstream reachability, `--json` for scripts.
Need the gateway on a fixed port? `codemie proxy start --port 4001 --profile work` launches the daemon by hand.
Done for the day? `codemie proxy stop` shuts the local gateway daemon down cleanly.
Unwiring Codex Desktop? `codemie proxy disconnect --codex-desktop` removes the CodeMie block from its config.
Curious which models your profile can actually call? `codemie models list` spells them out.
Share an MCP server with your team: `codemie mcp add myserver https://example.com/mcp --scope project` stores it in repo config; `--scope user` keeps it personal.
Hand your agents new tools: `codemie mcp add myserver https://example.com/mcp` registers an MCP server through the built-in proxy.
`codemie mcp list` shows every registered MCP server, and `codemie mcp remove myserver` cleans one out.
Need to bridge a stdio MCP server to HTTP with OAuth? `codemie mcp-proxy <url>` handles the translation.
`codemie setup assistants --project MyProject --agent claude` registers platform assistants straight into your agent config.
Same trick for skills: `codemie setup skills --agent claude,codex` registers platform skills into those agents.
Skills teach your agent new tricks — `codemie skill list` shows yours, filterable with `--agent codemie-code`.
`codemie skill sync --target claude` copies your CodeMie skills into the agent config — `--dry-run` previews, `--clean` prunes stale copies.
Skill misbehaving? `codemie skill validate` checks every skill file and tells you exactly what is wrong.
There is a shared skill registry out there — browse it and grab what you like with `codemie skills add`.
Someone probably solved it already: `codemie skills find "pdf"` searches the EPAM and skills.sh catalogs — `--json` for scripts.
`codemie skills add owner/repo` installs from skills.sh — grab one skill with `-s name`, target agents with `-a claude`, skip prompts with `-y`.
Agents are extensible: `codemie plugin list` shows what plugins you can bolt on.
Have an Anthropic-format plugin folder? `codemie plugin install ./my-plugin` adds it; `codemie plugin disable my-plugin` mutes it without uninstalling.
Agents call `codemie hook` with a JSON event on stdin — try it yourself: `echo '{"session_id":"demo","hook_event_name":"SessionStart"}' | codemie hook`.
Every session fires SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks — that is where skill sync and metrics flushing happen automatically.
Want audible cues? Drop a .wav/.mp3 into sounds/<event> under your CodeMie home and try `codemie sound SessionStart`.
Sounds go beyond session edges: drop audio into sounds/Stop or sounds/PermissionRequest under your CodeMie home to hear pauses and permission asks.
Want audio cues out of the box? `codemie install claude --sounds` wires hook sounds in during installation.
Need a quick one-shot answer? `codemie --task "summarize this repo"` runs a single task and exits — handy in scripts.
Scripting around the CLI? Pass -s/--silent to hide the decorative output so stdout stays machine-readable.
Wondering where your tokens go? `codemie analytics` breaks down usage, costs and session history across all agents.
`codemie analytics --report --open` builds a self-contained HTML dashboard of your usage and opens it in the browser.
Slice the numbers: `codemie analytics --agent claude --last 7d --branch main`, then `--export csv -o report.csv` to share.
`codemie log` browses your past sessions and debug logs — and `codemie log follow` tails a live one.
Replay a past run: `codemie log list-sessions` finds it, then `codemie log session <id> -v` shows the full conversation.
Logs pile up — `codemie log clean --days 7 --dry-run` previews the purge; drop `--dry-run` when you mean it.
Running OpenCode? `codemie opencode-metrics --discover` sweeps your recent sessions and extracts their metrics.
There is a visual side too: `codemie codebase ui` opens your repo as an interactive graph.
Not everything here is an agent — codebase-memory, codegraph and graphify are docs and knowledge tools; `codemie docs list` shows what is available.
Hidden gem: docs tools install one level down — `codemie docs install codegraph` gets you local code intelligence (codebase-memory and graphify work the same way).
Installed a docs tool? `codemie docs init codegraph` wires it into the current project, MCP config included.
CI without the YAML grind: `codemie workflow install pr-review` adds automated PR review to your repo — GitHub Actions or GitLab CI.
`codemie workflow list` shows the templates (pr-review, inline-fix, code-ci); `codemie workflow install pr-review -i` walks you through the options.
Big PRs need room to think: `codemie workflow install pr-review --timeout 30 --max-turns 100` raises the limits.
Prefer a guided conversation? `codemie assistants chat` connects you to your CodeMie assistants, interactively.
Script it instead: `codemie assistants chat <assistant-id> "Summarize this sprint"` sends one message and prints the reply.
Attach files to the chat: `codemie assistants chat <id> "Review these" -f ./report.pdf -f ./data.csv`.
Every platform asset answers to the same pattern — `codemie sdk assistants list`, `codemie sdk datasources list`, `codemie sdk integrations list`.
The platform is scriptable: `codemie sdk assistants list --scope marketplace --json` — narrow with `--search` and `--project`.
`codemie sdk llm list` shows the LLM catalog your CodeMie platform exposes.
Have a skill in markdown? `codemie sdk skills import ./my-skill.md` uploads it to the platform (needs YAML frontmatter with name and description).
Something feels off? `codemie doctor` health-checks your whole setup in seconds.
Reporting a bug? Grab your exact build first with `codemie version` — it saves everyone time.
Metrics not showing up? `codemie test-metrics` pings the CodeMie endpoint to check connectivity.
Curious what telemetry says about you? `codemie test-metrics --dry-run` shows the exact payload without sending anything.
When things misbehave, set CODEMIE_DEBUG=true to stream the debug log right into your console.
